label: On the word right after me, us or you that opens a description of that speaker or listener (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my', 'our' or 'your') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has I, we or you characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, criticising or thanking them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise the same I, we or you in return, whether the returned description matches the first one or is different or opposite. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns; named people are mostly silent. Silent: a returned attitude with no description after the pronoun (they trusted us); a returned description with no linking word, just a bare noun; a one-way characterisation with no earlier clause; the speaker characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, criticising or thanking them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in return, whether the returned description matches the first one or is different or opposite. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.
